name: Actor_IsGimmickTriggerUnfired
summary: Returns whether the gimmick trigger id stored at actor+0x2B8 has not yet been set in the field-trigger save bitmask; IsThereGimmickFixedItem uses the result to decide whether a fixed/gimmick item pickup is still available.
evidence: Disassembly shows r0 from callee 0x0066B3B0 surviving (`pop {r3,r4,r5,pc}`), so Ghidra dropped the returned value and 0x0066B3B0 is a getter returning !bit. That callee is the field-trigger bit test bounded by 0x306 (FACTS: trigger bitmask at bag+0x5418). The only genuine caller, IsThereGimmickFixedItem, calls it for the two fixed-item class tokens; 'SetBagSlotId' was wrong on both counts (not a setter, no bag slot).

name: maybe_Actor_IsGimmickTriggerUnfiredB
summary: Same field-trigger bit test as 0x00640D08 but for the actor's second u16 id at +0x2EC; IsThereGimmickFixedItem calls it for the other fixed-item class token.
evidence: Body is byte-for-byte 0x00640D08 with +0x2EC instead of +0x2B8, and the return register survives the call, i.e. it returns a value (getter) from the same 0x0066B3B0 trigger-bit test. Kept maybe_ because whether +0x2EC is a second trigger id or a region-book id is still unproven.

name: maybe_Item_GetNameVariantFlags
summary: Resolves the record selected by item+0x10 (masked with 0x7FFF) in the 0x0063E998 table and classifies it against the work bitmask at +0x2A2C8: 2 when the record's fourth u16 id is set, 1 when any of the first three ids is set, else 0.
evidence: Disassembly confirms the four bit tests read record offsets +0xC/+8/+4/+0 and the item selector is +0xA & 0x7FFF; the record/table role and whether the bits mean ownership remain unproven, so the old name is kept with a precise summary.

name: maybe_Party_MemberFlagPairA
summary: Tests the actor/leader flag word at +0x74 against a two-bit pair selected by the saved bytes at work+0x27C5A/+0x27C5B (0x10 or 0x20, and 0x1000 or 0x800). Camera_UpdateManualYaw uses it to decide whether the current leader belongs to the yaw-bias group.
evidence: Genuine caller Camera_UpdateManualYaw passes the player object at (work+8)->f_C and uses the result to add the manual yaw bias. The other callers listed by xref actually target the adjacent function 0x0066A6BC (handle-validity check), so there is still no named evidence for what the two global selector bytes mean.

name: maybe_Party_MemberFlagPairB
summary: Complement of 0x0066A604: tests the other two-bit pair (0x20/0x10 and 0x800/0x1000, selected by the same work+0x27C5A/B bytes) in the actor flag word at +0x74.
evidence: Exact complement of 0x0066A604 and used by Camera_UpdateManualYaw for the opposite yaw-bias branch. The long caller list in the dossier (Gfx_SceneSpriteSet/Ui_SceneFlow helpers) belongs to the adjacent 0x0066A6BC handle check, not to this function.

name: Ui_Object_OnEventApplyStoryFlag
summary: Virtual event handler for the UI object whose embedded slide window starts at +0x258: it forwards the event to Ui_SlideWindow_OnEventB and, for event id 6, sets the sub-object at -0x20C according to one of three story/global flag bytes selected by object+0x2C8.
evidence: Disassembly shows `sub r5,r0,#0x258` before the Ui_SlideWindow_OnEventB call, so this is a sibling of the named Ui_Object_OnEventPathOrToggle (0x0066E5FC) on the same UI object; the only special case is event==6. 'Actor' was wrong because the receiver is clearly a UI object.

name: maybe_Party_RemoveMemberAndRelease
summary: Teardown of a party member's field actor: unregisters the two level-map cell ids at self->f_298 (+0x1A/+0x1C) through 0x006136BC, releases the actor's attached objects and calls its +0x58/+0x40 virtual methods with 4.
evidence: The body is a release path: 0x006136BC scans the 40-entry map-cell table at bag+0x4DD8 and clears matching ids, then Actor_ReleaseAttachedObjects runs. The Party attribution still rests on self->f_298 and the old evidence, so it stays at 0.4.

name: maybe_Party_RemoveAllMembersAndRelease
summary: Bulk teardown variant: clears the shared name/actor table at bag+0x92F4 through 0x00192DE4, then releases the actor's attached objects and calls its +0x58/+0x40 virtual methods with 4.
evidence: Same release tail as 0x00670668, but the cell unregister is replaced by 0x00192DE4, which walks the 0x55-entry name table at bag+0x92F4 clearing 0xFF entries. The 'all members' reading remains plausible but unproven.

name: maybe_Party_RemoveMemberAndReleaseB
summary: Second single-member teardown: unregisters the level-map cell pair from self->f_298 (u16 at +2 and byte at +0xC) through 0x006136BC, then releases the actor objects and calls the same +0x58/+0x40 slots.
evidence: Twin of 0x00670668 with different f_298 offsets (u16 +2 / byte +0xC instead of +0x1A/+0x1C), which fits a second object/cell layout; there is still no named caller, so the Party prefix is kept tentative.

name: maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_ShowSelectionText
summary: Refreshes the shop window's description text for the selected id at f_238: resolves the id twice through 0x006131B0/0x00613410, builds the text id with 0x00210A50(3) and stores it in the message pair at f_4BC.
evidence: The recovered body shows the two table lookups and the f_4BC message-pair write; that pair is created by the named Ui_BoushiShopWindow_InitPanes, which supports the shop-window attribution, but no named caller proves the class.

name: Ui_FindRowByCurrentKey
summary: Searches the 0x1C-byte row table reached through self+0x44/f_58 for the row whose u16 key equals the current key at work+0x27C5C; if absent it returns the first row whose key is 0xFFFF (free slot), otherwise NULL.
evidence: Disassembly shows the stride-0x1C scan (`add r0,r0,#0x1C`), the key load from work+0x27C5C and the 0xFFFF fallback, exactly matching the old name; the two named callers are message-window/field-screen users of the same row table.

name: maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: One step of the dialog page-transition state machine: checks the pending-command mask at +0x480 (& 0x142/4/1) and dispatches transition codes 2/4/5/6/8/9/10 through the page vtable at +0x11C.
evidence: The recovered body is a self-contained page-transition dispatcher with a named page object at +0x378; the four-row list and the two sibling variants remain unverified, so the dialog wording is retained only as maybe_.

name: Ui_PartyStatus_ResetValue
signature: void Ui_PartyStatus_ResetValue(UiPartyStatusPanel* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 context)
summary: Resets one party-status gauge: clears status bit 0x80 on the member record selected by self->f_768, zeroes the record's +0x1C2 and the panel's displayed value at +0x118.
evidence: The named callee Ui_PartyStatus_ApplyValue and the sibling Ui_PartyStatus_* cluster confirm the panel; disassembly of 0x001902A4 shows a `bic` clear of member+0xDA (Ghidra's Member_RemoveItemAtSlot xref is a nearest-symbol artefact), so reset-value is supported.

name: Ui_PartyStatus_CommitValue
signature: void Ui_PartyStatus_CommitValue(UiPartyStatusPanel* party, u32 old, u32 arg3, u32 context)
summary: Commits a gauge change: when the target value differs it clears the member flag 0x80, resets the icon index and animates the bar through vtable +0xE4/+0x120/+0x178, with the 'value > 0x120' special case.
evidence: The named callee Ui_PartyStatus_ApplyValue and the same member-record/gauge fields place this in the party-status panel; the commit/animate flow is fully readable, so the old guess is confirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_HighlightList_ApplyMapState
summary: Shared highlight updater: walks 32 8-byte records at self+0x8F4 (element pointer, u16 map id, expected state) and sets bit 0 of element+0x44 when the per-map state byte at bag+0x2A70+mapId equals the record's expected state.
evidence: The named callers are unrelated (Ui_MonsterBook_FillEntry, Ui_NpcIcon_UpdateFromRecord, maybe_Anim2D_RebindRecordTable), so this is a shared record-list helper rather than a world-map-marker method; 'WorldMapMarker' was too narrow.

name: maybe_Ui_FourRowList_ResetFromStateA
summary: Wrapper around the four-row list reset: reads one word from the global context and the map-state value from 0x0066BAC4(bag), then passes both to maybe_Ui_FourRowList_Reset.
evidence: The recovered body is a two-constant wrapper around the still-maybe four-row reset; its caller is the dialog page-transition variant, but neither the list class nor the state word is named.

name: maybe_Ui_FourRowList_ResetFromStateB
summary: Second wrapper around the same four-row reset, identical to 0x003F6F20 but reading context offset 0x003F72CC and map-state getter 0x0066BA6C.
evidence: Byte-for-byte twin of 0x003F6F20 except for the two constants; called by the other dialog page-transition variant, but the list/state meaning is still unproven.

name: Item_ComputePriceWithMultiplier
signature: u32 Item_ComputePriceWithMultiplier(const void* record, const void* row, u32 count)
summary: Computes a price as count * record->f_228 * the u16 at row+4, scales it by 2^record->f_22C, then clamps the result so that the counter at bag+0x31F4 entry 0 plus the price does not exceed 9,999,999.
evidence: The multiply/shift and the 0x98967F cap check are explicit in the body; the cap is the same 9,999,999 limit used by the shop helpers, so the price-with-multiplier reading is confirmed. Ghidra dropped the u32 return value.

name: maybe_Field_GetActorTableValue
summary: Getter for one of the static u16 entries selected by index; the callee 0x005BCA28 ignores the work-bag argument and returns an entry from the 10-entry table at rodata 0x007843DC.
evidence: Disassembly of 0x005BCA28 overwrites r1 and indexes a 10-entry u16 table at rodata 0x007843DC, so the old 'NotifyActor' name was wrong; the callers fill render display params, but the table's meaning is still unknown.

name: Party_Member_AddHP
summary: Adds delta to the party member's current HP at +0x14 through virtual slot 0 (the HP setter/clamp).
evidence: FACTS gives PartyMember +0x14 = HP and +0x10 = max HP; this helper resolves the member via 0x0035EB98 and passes +0x14 + delta to vt[0], while its getter counterpart returns +0x14.

name: Party_Member_AddMP
summary: Adds delta to the party member's current MP at +0x16 and clamps it to the maximum MP at +0x12 (0..max).
evidence: FACTS gives +0x12 = max MP from Party_Member_RecalculateStats and +0x16 = current MP; the clamp pair here is exactly the MP pair, unlike the +0x10/+0x14 HP pair.

name: Work_GetGold
summary: Tail-call getter for the party wallet: returns entry 0 of the u32 counter array at bag+0x31F4, the gold value the amount spinner clamps against the 9,999,999 cap.
evidence: R_010 verified 0x0066B2CC(work,i) = work[i*4+0x31F4]; Ui_AmountSpinner_Step (0x003D28FC) reads entry 0 as the wallet and clamps amount+wallet to 0x0098967F. Disassembly shows the callee's r0 surviving, so this is a getter (Ghidra dropped the return). GetGold (0x001633B4) exposes the canonical bag+0x28 field, but the spinner uses this counter-array copy.

name: Party_Member_SetHP
summary: Sets the party member's current HP (+0x14) through virtual slot 0, the same setter used by the HP add helper.
evidence: Resolves the member via 0x0035EB98 and calls vt[0] with the value; FACTS identifies +0x14 as HP and vt[+0x08] as the max-HP getter, so slot 0 is the HP setter.

name: Party_Member_SetMP
summary: Sets the party member's current MP at +0x16, clamped to the maximum MP at +0x12.
evidence: Same +0x12/+0x16 clamp pair as Party_Member_AddMP; FACTS identifies +0x12 as max MP and +0x16 as current MP.

name: maybe_Field_SetModeByte
summary: Stores a single byte in the work block at +0x27C7B; no callers, so the meaning of the byte is unknown.
evidence: Only the destination byte changed hands since the first pass; no named caller or callee identifies the mode, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_CheckPositionAndTrigger
signature: void maybe_Field_CheckPositionAndTrigger(u32 x, u32 y, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Compares the saved map position (x,y packed in the high halves of the two words from 0x0066B5F8) with x/y, and on a match forwards the trigger parameters to 0x0035F0C4 with mode 1.
evidence: Coordinate comparison is clear, but 0x0035F0C4 and 0x0066B5F8 are still unnamed and there are no genuine callers. The predicate-name flag does not apply: the body performs the trigger as a side effect and returns no value.

name: maybe_Party_Member_InvokeVtableSlot1
summary: Resolves the party member and invokes virtual slot 1 with no arguments; if slot 0 is the HP setter, slot 1 is most likely the MP update/reset virtual.
evidence: Only the member resolution and vtable index +8 are knowable from the body; no caller or sibling names slot 1, so the action stays unknown.

name: Party_Member_GetMaxMP
summary: Returns the party member's maximum MP (+0x12).
evidence: FACTS: Party_Member_RecalculateStats writes max MP at +0x12; this getter resolves the member via 0x0035EB98 and returns that field.

name: maybe_Field_SetStat
summary: Guarded write of a per-index stat word: when not in event mode it stores value through 0x00612B08 into the u32 array at bag+0x2998.
evidence: Disassembly of 0x00612B08 confirms the `str r2,[bag + index*4 + 0x2998]` store; the index space and stat meaning are still unknown, so it stays maybe_.

name: Field_SetFlagBit
summary: Sets bit 0 of the per-index flag byte at bag+0x5762 (indices < 0x65) by calling 0x00612550.
evidence: Disassembly of 0x00612550 is `ldrb r1,[bag+index+0x5762]; orr r1,#1; strb`, exactly a bit-0 setter; the wrapper does no other work.

name: Party_Member_GetHP
summary: Returns the party member's current HP (+0x14).
evidence: FACTS gives +0x14 as HP; this getter resolves the member via 0x0035EB98 and returns that field, the same value Party_Member_AddHP modifies.

name: Party_Member_GetMP
summary: Returns the party member's current MP (+0x16).
evidence: FACTS gives +0x16 as current MP (max at +0x12); this getter returns it after resolving the member via 0x0035EB98.

name: Field_TestFlagBit
summary: Returns bit 0 of the per-index flag byte at bag+0x5762 (indices < 0x65) through 0x0066B004.
evidence: Disassembly of 0x0066B004 returns `byte[bag+index+0x5762] & 1`; Ghidra typed the wrapper void but r0 survives, so this returns a value and is the getter counterpart of Field_SetFlagBit. The old 'SetState' was the opposite operation.

name: maybe_Party_SpendResource
summary: Damaged Thumb routine that reads counter slot 10 (bag+0x2998 array via 0x0066B0F8) and, when the signed amount is negative, raises it to -amount through 0x00612B08; the leading 0x00613FC0 call adjusts the bag.
evidence: Body is damaged (unaff_r4/r6) but the hard-coded slot 10 and the 0x0066B0F8/0x00612B08 pair are legible; no callers, so the resource meaning stays a guess.

name: Party_Member_SetStatusFlag
summary: Sets a party-member status bit: ORs flags into member+0xDA through 0x00192414; flag 0x80 is skipped when already set, while flag 0x10 replaces the word, matching the shared status-flag setter.
evidence: The helper 0x00192414 is a status-flag OR with special cases 0x10/0x08, and this wrapper resolves a party member via 0x0035EB98 before calling it; 'EnsureVisible' described only one possible bit.

name: maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance2
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance2(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Second dialog page-transition variant: uses the alternate page object at +0x3C4, resets it through maybe_Ui_FourRowList_ResetFromStateB, and sends page command 7 after 0x006122F0(bag,id) when the pending id at +0x468 is set.
evidence: Twin of 0x00166DBC with a different page object; both callers and callees are unverified, so the dialog wording is kept only as maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance3
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_DialogAdvance3(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Third dialog page-transition variant: reads the mask at +0x120, resets the four-row page through maybe_Ui_FourRowList_ResetFromStateA and dispatches page commands 1/3 through the vtable at self+0x47.
evidence: The body has overlapping/bad instructions and unaff registers, so only the dispatch shape is trustworthy; kept at low confidence.

name: Party_BuildActorIndex
signature: u32* Party_BuildActorIndex(u32* out, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Builds the global actor-id -> party-slot reverse index at 0x007C6E7C: for slots 0..0x1E it reads the id from bag+i+4 and stores the slot under that id; also initialises the small output descriptor.
evidence: The loop bound 0x1F, the id source 0x0066B0E4(bag,i) and the global index writes are explicit; the actor-id/party-slot mapping is exactly what the old name said, only the id source's name is still vague.

name: Text_ResolveStyleBlock
summary: Resolves a 16-word text style block: fills the 7-wchar name at +4 from party member 0 when empty, refreshes level (+0x38) and three global bytes (+0x34/+0x3D/+0x3E), allocates the formatted name buffer and returns whether anything changed. maybe_Text_UpdateStyleParams calls it before 0x00613F14 applies the block to the text object.
evidence: Disassembly shows wcslen (0x00100B74) is a CRT call, not a noreturn throw (FACTS trap), followed by the name copy from member+0xCA, level from member+0xD8, allocations through 0x0011CFAC/0x00116AE0 and a changed-flag return. N_010/N_022 context describes the same function as the style resolver called from 0x00193248. This is text/style code, not item code.

name: maybe_Field_SetModeValue
summary: Stores an int at bag+0x8760 and, when the new value is 0, clears the 0x108-byte state block at bag+0x8630 first via 0x00111498.
evidence: Both the store offset and the 0x00111498 block clear are confirmed from disassembly, but no caller identifies what the value selects; kept maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_BuildStatusList
signature: void maybe_Ui_BuildStatusList(void* self, int* ids, u32 arg3, int count)
summary: Fills a UI list from up to 8 ids (stops at -1): each entry becomes {id, u16 value from work+id*0x8C+0x2AAF4}, then stores the count at +0x6C and notifies the list vtable.
evidence: The id/value pairing and the 0x8C actor-record stride are clear; the 'status' wording still rests on the unnamed callers, so it stays maybe_.

name: Ui_PartyStatus_AddMPPreview
signature: void Ui_PartyStatus_AddMPPreview(UiPartyStatusPanel* party, s16 delta, u32 arg3, u32 context)
summary: Adjusts a party-status gauge preview: adds delta to the member's MP (+0x16, clamped to max MP +0x12) and to the panel's displayed value at +0x36 (clamped to +0x32), guarded by the global UI-busy bytes.
evidence: The member clamp pair is the known MP pair (+0x12/+0x16) and the panel fields mirror it; the two guards and the named Ui_PartyStatus_* cluster support the party-status attribution.

name: maybe_Ui_PartyStatus_ClearFlag10
signature: void maybe_Ui_PartyStatus_ClearFlag10(UiPartyStatusPanel* party, u32 value, u32 arg3, u32 context)
summary: Clears status bit 0x10 on the selected member record and forwards value to the panel gauge through vtable +0x3C.
evidence: Disassembly of 0x001902A4 is a `bic` (clear) of the mask, not a set, so 'SetFlag10' was the wrong direction; the meaning of bit 0x10 remains unknown, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Message_FormatTextArg
signature: void maybe_Message_FormatTextArg(int text, int arg2, int arg3, int context)
summary: Thumb message-argument formatter: walks the 8-byte argument-table entries (u16 tags at +4/+6, 0xFF terminator) and applies the font/colour variant of the matching tag. This is message text code, not item code.
evidence: The register-damaged body still shows the same table walk as the named formatter; Ghidra lost the argument registers, so the name is kept at low confidence.

name: maybe_Save_SetMinBytes
signature: u32 maybe_Save_SetMinBytes(u32 index, int value, u32 arg3, u32 context)
summary: Writes a 9-byte persistent block back to work+0x2D385 only when the incoming byte is smaller than the stored one; returns whether it wrote.
evidence: Register-damaged Thumb body; the min comparison and the 9-byte block copy are legible but the block's meaning is unknown, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Save_GetBlockByteEquals3
signature: u32 maybe_Save_GetBlockByteEquals3(u32 index, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 context)
summary: Returns whether the persistent byte at work+0x2D385+index equals 3 (the 'fully unlocked/upgraded' recipe state used by the forge screen).
evidence: The comparison and caller (Ui_RecipeBook_ChooseStateByItemFlags) are unchanged; renaming from the address-based 'GetFlagEquals3' to the actual block offset is more accurate, but the block is still unnamed.

name: maybe_Save_TestProgressMask
signature: u32 maybe_Save_TestProgressMask(u8 mask, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 context)
summary: Tests a bit mask against the progress byte at bag+0x88F7; the recipe-book refresh uses masks 1/2/4.
evidence: The byte location and the 1/2/4 masks used by the named recipe-book refresh are clear, but what the three bits mean is not.

name: Flag_GetGlobal1
summary: Returns whether the global flag byte at work+0x27509 (index 1 of the flag block based at 0x27508) is set.
evidence: Named Flag_GetGlobalIndexed (0x001A5AE4) reads the same block via an id->offset table, and the recipe-book refresh uses this fixed index-1 flag as one of its three unlock conditions; '27509' was only an address, not a meaning.

name: Save_OrBlockBits
summary: ORs a mask into the last byte of the 9-byte persistent block at work+0x2D385 (reads the block, ORs the byte at +0x2D38F, writes it back).
evidence: The body copies the 9-byte block and ORs the mask into the final byte at +0x2D38F, exactly the old description; this is the same block the recipe-book helpers use.

name: maybe_Party_SetSelectedMember
signature: void maybe_Party_SetSelectedMember(void* party, u8 member, u32 arg3, u32 context)
summary: Stores the selected member index at self+0x24A and bumps the bag counter at +0x30 (unless it is -1) through 0x00612D40.
evidence: The field store and the counter bump are clear, but no caller exists and 0x00612D40 is a generic counter increment, so the 'selected member' meaning is still inferred.
